topics.en: Food and Three Meals a Day

example.en: I eat fried noodles for lunch.
We eat snacks together in the afternoon.
I eat a late-night snack at ten o'clock at night.
I can speak a little Chinese.
Please take the medicine on time.
I am going to the pharmacy to buy medicine.
I am going to the post office to mail a letter.
The police station is near the school.
I eat pasta in the evening.

vocab.en: eat; make a living by relying on something

grammar.name: 刚刚在动词
grammar.explanationEn: 刚刚在动词 is used to indicate that an action has just happened, typically describing something that occurred a very short time ago.

grammar.name: 还没还没有动词
grammar.explanationEn: “还没” or “还没有” is used to indicate that an action or state has not yet occurred or been completed. It is often used to describe the current situation and implies that it might happen or be completed in the future.

grammar.name: 主语时间地点动作
grammar.explanationEn: In Chinese, the basic sentence structure is: Subject + Time + Place + Action. This word order helps clearly express who did what, when, and where.

grammar.name: 的时候
grammar.explanationEn: “的时候” is used to indicate a specific point or period of time when something happens. It connects the main clause and the time adverbial clause, showing an action or state occurring at a certain time.

example.zh: 吃饭的时候，我喜欢看电视。
example.en: When eating, I like to watch TV.

grammar.name: 跟人一起或动词
grammar.explanationEn: ‘跟人一起或动词’ indicates doing something together with someone, emphasizing collaboration or joint participation. ‘跟’ means ‘with,’ and ‘一起’ means ‘together,’ followed by a verb.

grammar.name: 可以 vs 能不能
grammar.explanationEn: “可以” means permission or possibility, often used to express allowance or ability. “能不能” is an interrogative form, used to ask whether someone has the ability or is allowed to do something.

example.en: Can I go to the restroom?

grammar.name: 省略成分
grammar.explanationEn: In sentences, omitted components refer to omitting unnecessary words or parts for simplicity or to avoid repetition. For example, when the context is clear, the subject, object, or other parts can be omitted.

grammar.name: 什么在疑问句中的用法
grammar.explanationEn: “什么” is an interrogative pronoun used to ask about things, content, or information. It is typically used in interrogative sentences to mean 'what thing' or 'what matter'.
